children: Italy's economy grew by 0.2% in the second quarter from the previous three months, boosted by domestic demand that offset a negative contribution from trade flows, national statistics bureau ISTAT said on Tuesday, confirming a previous printout.
Year-on-year, second quarter gross domestic product in the euro zone's third largest economy increased by 1.0%, also confirming the estimate made by ISTAT on July 30.

Exports grew by 0.8% in the second quarter compared with January-March, against a 1.7% increase in imports, with net trade subtracting 0.3 percentage points from the quarterly growth rate, ISTAT said.
Consumer spending, inventories and investments all increased.

Giorgia Meloni's government in April cut its growth outlook to 0.6% for both this year and next, reflecting surging energy prices and turmoil in the Middle East, from previous targets of 0.7% and 0.8% respectively.
However, Italian economic data has held up better than expected since then, and so-called "acquired growth" stood at 0.8% at the end of the April-June period, ISTAT said.
This means that even if GDP is flat in each of the remaining two quarters of 2026, full-year growth will be up 0.8% from 2025.
Italian GDP rose 0.5% in 2025, a third straight year of sub-1% growth.
ISTAT confirmed that in the first quarter the economy expanded 0.3% quarter-on-quarter and 0.8% year-on-year.
